title: Formal nodal completed stalks, canonical scalar maps, and hypersurface models
statement: In one scheme universe, for a scheme $X$ and point $x$ [def-pc-scheme], write $C(X,x)=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$ for the maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The formal nodal constructions are the following explicit rings, maps, and scalar structures. (1) The completed stalk is $C(X,x)$. (2) For a commutative ring $R$, a morphism $g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $x\in X$, the coefficient map $R\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the canonical map $R\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,g(x)}$ followed by $g_x^\#$. (3) For $f:X\to Y$ and $t\in X$, put $s=f(t)$ and regard $t$ as its canonical point $t_f$ in the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Equip $C(X_s,t_f)$ with its $\kappa(s)$-algebra structure [def-weil-residue-field] by the coefficient map of $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ followed by completion. (4) Equip $C(X,t)$ with its $C(Y,s)$-algebra structure via the completion of the local stalk map $\mathcal O_{Y,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,t}$: in coordinate $n$ it sends the class of $a$ to the class of $f_t^\#(a)$ modulo the $n$th power of the target maximal ideal. (5) For any commutative ring $R$ and $h\in R$, put $Q(R,h)=R[[u,v]]/(uv-h)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], with $u,v$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(2)$ and constants embedded by the power-series coefficient map. (6) Put $P(R,h)=R[u,v]/(uv-h)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with the same variable indexing and the polynomial coefficient map. (7) Put $M(R,h)=\operatorname{Spec}P(R,h)$. (8) For a commutative local ring $A$, write $\widehat A$ for its maximal-ideal completion and $\mathfrak m_A$ for its maximal ideal. For $h\in\widehat A$, define the origin ideal in $P(\widehat A,h)$ as the image of $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A[u,v]+(u,v)$ under $\widehat A[u,v]\to P(\widehat A,h)$. This is an ideal, with no assertion here that it is prime or that $h$ lies in a maximal ideal. (9) For a commutative ring $R$, $h\in R$, and $o\in M(R,h)$, equip $C(M(R,h),o)$ with its $R$-algebra structure by $R\to P(R,h)\to\mathcal O_{M(R,h),o}\to C(M(R,h),o)$. These are definitions only; no formal local structure isomorphism or algebraization theorem is asserted.
